guidance.requirement: Ensure leadership follows through on intended ISMS outcomes.
guidance.context: Describe how management notices shortfalls and acts on them. Having a dashboard without management attention is insufficient.

guidance.requirement: Direct and support people's contribution to ISMS effectiveness.
guidance.context: Discuss actual support for people doing security-related work; this can be practical direction and problem resolution.

guidance.requirement: Support relevant managers in demonstrating security leadership.
guidance.context: Consider how managers receive authority and support in their own areas. No particular management hierarchy is required.

guidance.requirement: Promote continual improvement of the ISMS.
guidance.context: Describe how management encourages useful changes and acts on improvement opportunities. A separate improvement committee is optional.

guidance.requirement: Include commitment to continual ISMS improvement.
guidance.context: Check management's stated direction. A particular policy title or declaration template is not required.

guidance.requirement: Make the information security policy available as documented information.
guidance.context: An accessible controlled policy page or another suitable format can work. A signed paper file is not the only option.

guidance.requirement: Communicate the security policy within the organization.
guidance.context: Explain how affected people receive the current direction. An awareness platform or annual acknowledgement is not required by this question.

guidance.requirement: Make the policy appropriately available to interested parties.
guidance.context: Use actual relationship needs. Controlled sharing or a suitable published version can be appropriate; making the full internal policy public is not universally required.

guidance.context: Trace a relevant business condition into planning. Climate relevance can be one input, without implying a separate climate-control program.

guidance.requirement: Use relevant interested-party requirements in ISMS planning.
guidance.context: Use actual interested-party requirements, not assumed obligations based on a client label.

guidance.requirement: Determine risks requiring attention in ISMS planning.
guidance.context: Consider risks to the management system's ability to work as intended. This complements the information-security risk method in 6.1.2.

guidance.requirement: Determine opportunities requiring attention in ISMS planning.
guidance.context: Consider useful opportunities to strengthen the management system. A separate opportunity register or invented project is optional.

guidance.requirement: Address risks and opportunities needed for intended ISMS outcomes.
guidance.context: Explain what success the planning choices protect. The organization's actual intended outcomes provide the reference.

guidance.requirement: Address prevention or reduction of unwanted effects.
guidance.context: Explain the effects planning is intended to prevent or reduce. Eliminating every possible risk is not implied.

guidance.requirement: Address risks and opportunities needed for continual improvement.
guidance.context: Discuss how the planned response supports improvement, without assuming a particular improvement project.

guidance.requirement: Plan actions addressing selected risks and opportunities.
guidance.context: Describe a practicable response using existing plans or work records. This asks about chosen actions, not a prescribed plan template.

guidance.requirement: Plan integration of the actions into ISMS processes.
guidance.context: Explain the connection to existing operational or management activities. A standalone action list without an integration plan leaves this unclear.

guidance.requirement: Plan implementation of the actions through the ISMS.
guidance.context: Describe the organization's intended delivery approach. A new project-management product is optional.

guidance.requirement: Plan evaluation of the actions' effectiveness.
guidance.context: Explain what would show the response worked. Fixed monthly, quarterly or annual intervals are not introduced here.

requirement.text: A repeatable risk assessment approach makes criteria, ownership and evaluation consistent enough to support meaningful decisions.

guidance.requirement: Define the information security risk-assessment process.
guidance.context: Explain the steps assessors follow. A qualitative, quantitative or mixed approach may work when it supports the required decisions.

guidance.requirement: Apply the defined risk-assessment process.
guidance.context: Compare the method with completed assessments. Buying a risk tool or approving a method without using it is insufficient.

guidance.requirement: Retain documented information about the risk-assessment process.
guidance.context: An accessible procedure or equivalent controlled record can work. A particular methodology name is optional.

guidance.requirement: Establish information security risk-acceptance criteria.
guidance.context: Explain how acceptable and unacceptable risk are distinguished. A numeric threshold is one option, not a universal requirement.

guidance.requirement: Maintain information security risk-acceptance criteria.
guidance.context: Explain how the adopted criteria remain usable for current decisions. No universal review interval is prescribed here.

guidance.requirement: Establish criteria for performing information security risk assessments.
guidance.context: Explain the agreed basis for assessors' decisions, such as scales or evaluation rules appropriate to the organization.

guidance.requirement: Maintain the criteria for performing risk assessments.
guidance.context: Discuss whether current assessments still use appropriate criteria. Replacing criteria without understanding earlier results may undermine comparison.

guidance.requirement: Resolve inconsistency in repeated risk assessments.
guidance.context: Consider whether assessors apply the agreed criteria in a consistent way. Examples or calibration discussions can help explain the answer.

guidance.requirement: Resolve weaknesses affecting the validity of risk-assessment results.
guidance.context: Consider whether judgments are grounded in actual circumstances and meaningful criteria. Automated scores are not automatically valid.

guidance.requirement: Make repeated risk-assessment results meaningfully comparable.
guidance.context: Explain how changes in assumptions or criteria are understood when comparing results. No specific risk-scoring system is required.

guidance.requirement: Identify confidentiality-loss risks to in-scope information.
guidance.context: Consider inappropriate access or disclosure using actual information and relationships. An asset-first or scenario-first method can both work.

guidance.requirement: Identify integrity-loss risks to in-scope information.
guidance.context: Consider unwanted alteration, corruption or loss of trust in information. Do not assume every risk is only a cyberattack.

guidance.requirement: Identify availability-loss risks to in-scope information.
guidance.context: Consider inability to access needed information or services. Use the organization's actual service dependencies.

guidance.requirement: Cover in-scope information in risk identification.
guidance.context: Consider important interfaces and externally provided services as well as internal activities. A limited assessment sample does not define the whole scope.

guidance.requirement: Identify the owners of information security risks.
guidance.context: Explain who is responsible for each risk. An individual or appropriate accountable role can work; an optional contact name is not the duty being assessed.

guidance.requirement: Assess potential consequences of identified risks.
guidance.context: Use the possible effects on the organization if the scenario occurs. A qualitative impact description can be suitable.

guidance.requirement: Assess realistic likelihood of identified risks.
guidance.context: Explain assumptions using actual conditions and available information. A precise probability is not inherently required.

guidance.requirement: Determine risk levels using the adopted analysis method.
guidance.context: Explain how the organization's method produces the level used for decisions. A particular scoring formula is optional.

guidance.requirement: Compare analyzed risks with established risk criteria.
guidance.context: Explain how the comparison informs a decision about the assessed risk. A score without evaluation does not answer this question.

guidance.requirement: Prioritize analyzed risks for treatment.
guidance.context: Describe how the evaluation determines attention or sequence. The interview does not impose a specific ordering formula.

guidance.requirement: Define the information security risk-treatment process.
guidance.context: Explain how assessed risks lead to treatment decisions. Use the existing risk workflow where appropriate.

guidance.requirement: Apply the defined risk-treatment process.
guidance.context: Trace an actual decision from assessment to treatment. A plan template without use does not demonstrate application.

guidance.requirement: Select appropriate treatment options using assessment results.
guidance.context: Different responses can be appropriate for different risks. Do not equate acceptance with automatic completion of every control.

guidance.requirement: Determine the controls necessary for chosen treatments.
guidance.context: Consider controls designed by the organization or selected from any suitable source. Necessary controls can extend beyond Annex A.

guidance.requirement: Compare necessary controls with the Annex A reference set.
guidance.context: The comparison is a safeguard against omissions; it does not make every Annex A control universally necessary. Existing mapping records can support it.

guidance.requirement: Check the comparison for omitted necessary controls.
guidance.context: Explain how unmatched reference controls or treatment gaps were considered. A completed mapping alone does not establish that omissions were evaluated.

guidance.requirement: Include necessary controls in the Statement of Applicability.
guidance.context: Use the organization's selected controls, including custom or non-Annex controls. An Annex-only list can omit necessary treatments.

guidance.requirement: Record justification for including necessary controls.
guidance.context: Reasons may reflect risk, obligations or other relevant needs. Presence in Annex A alone is not the organization's treatment rationale.

guidance.requirement: Record whether the necessary controls are implemented.

guidance.context: An integrated plan or linked treatment records can work when they provide the needed plan. A particular plan title or project tool is optional.

guidance.requirement: Obtain risk-owner approval of the treatment plan.
guidance.context: Check the owners' actual approval through the organization's appropriate process. Top management review alone does not substitute for risk-owner approval.

guidance.requirement: Obtain risk-owner acceptance of residual information security risks.
guidance.context: Discuss the remaining exposure and the owners' actual acceptance decision. A completed treatment action does not itself record residual-risk acceptance.

guidance.requirement: Retain documented information about the risk-treatment process.

requirement.text: Information security objectives need an accountable plan and measures that show whether progress is being made.
requirement.trigger: Set, monitor, communicate and update appropriate security objectives; plan responsibility, resources, completion timing and evaluation. Use each objective’s planned timing, not a forced annual cycle.

guidance.requirement: Establish security objectives at relevant functions and levels.
guidance.context: Use objectives appropriate to where work and decisions occur. Every team does not need a separate objective if that level is not relevant.

guidance.requirement: Align objectives with information security policy.
guidance.context: Explain how objectives reflect the adopted policy direction. A generic target list does not demonstrate that connection.

guidance.requirement: Make objectives measurable where practicable.
guidance.context: Use measures suited to the objective. Where measurement is impracticable, explain why and how achievement can be evaluated; a numeric KPI is not universally required.

guidance.requirement: Consider applicable security requirements when setting objectives.
guidance.context: Use actual obligations and requirements determined for the organization. Do not infer legal applicability from an interview answer.

guidance.requirement: Consider risk-assessment results when setting objectives.
guidance.context: Trace relevant assessed exposures into the chosen objectives where appropriate.

guidance.requirement: Consider risk-treatment results when setting objectives.
guidance.context: Consider the treatment decisions and remaining exposures affecting intended outcomes.

guidance.requirement: Monitor the security objectives.
guidance.context: Explain how progress is observed using suitable information. A dashboard is one option, and no universal monitoring interval is prescribed here.

guidance.requirement: Communicate the security objectives.
guidance.context: Consider the people who need to understand or contribute to the objectives. Existing meetings or written direction can work.

guidance.requirement: Update security objectives as appropriate.
guidance.context: Explain how the organization responds when objectives need to change. An annual rewrite is not inherently required.

guidance.context: A controlled page, plan or another suitable record can work. A dedicated objectives register is optional.

guidance.requirement: Retain documented information about the objectives.
guidance.context: Explain how records remain available rather than being lost as objectives change. This does not invent a retention period.

guidance.context: Explain the planned work supporting the objective, using existing plans where suitable.

guidance.requirement: Determine the resources needed to achieve each objective.
guidance.context: Consider the actual people, time, capabilities and other resources needed; a specific tool is optional.

guidance.requirement: Determine responsibility for achieving each objective.
guidance.context: Identify responsibility for delivery. The label of the role is flexible; responsibility itself is substantive.

guidance.requirement: Determine completion timing for objective achievement work.
guidance.context: Use a completion timeframe appropriate to the objective. The standard does not impose an identical deadline for all objectives.

guidance.requirement: Determine how objective results will be evaluated.
guidance.context: Explain how the organization will judge success. Finishing activities alone does not show whether an objective was achieved.
